messages.author: 1699b7ac1d44f721
messages.subject: NA issue with unmarkedMultFrame
parts:
Hi all,

I'm new to unmarked (having previously used ProgramMARK). I'm trying to run multi-season occupancy models using colext. When I run a summary on my unmarkedMultFrame, it seems like NAs are getting counted as 1s. Or at least it is determining that all 63 sites have at least one detection, which is incorrect. I've double checked my encounter history and verified that only 27 sites have at least one detection. When I replace NAs with a different character such as "-" or ".", the summary function correctly identifies the number of sites with at least one detection. The characters then get coerced back to NAs when the colext function is run but then I'm not quite confident that model output or predictions are correct (they don't seem like it) based on the fact that the unmarkedMultFrame seems to be 'misidentifying' the NAs in the first place.

*With NAs
 > head(occmatx)
[,14] [,15] [,16] [,17] [,18] [,19] [,20] [,21] [1,] "0" "0" "0" "NA" "NA" "NA" "NA" "NA" [2,] "0" "0" "0" "NA" "NA" "NA" "NA" "NA" [3,] "0" "0" "NA" "NA" "NA" "NA" "NA" "NA" [4,] "0" "0" "0" "0" "NA" "NA" "NA" "NA" [5,] "0" "0" "1" "0" "0" "0" "NA" "NA" [6,] "0" "0" "0" "0" "0" "0" "NA" "NA"

> head(stands) age_surv dist_of_s 1 31 646 2 27 0 3 97 0 4 27 2 5 28 27 6 56 0  

> rtv_umf <- unmarkedMultFrame(y=occmatx, siteCovs = stands, numPrimary = 4) > summary(rtv_umf) unmarkedFrame Object 63 sites Maximum number of observations per site: 116 Mean number of observations per site: 116 Number of primary survey periods: 4 Number of secondary survey periods: 29 Sites with at least one detection: 63 Tabulation of y observations: 0 1 NA 2683 92 4533 Site-level covariates: age_surv dist_of_s Min. : 21.0 Min. : 0.0 1st Qu.: 28.5 1st Qu.: 0.0 Median : 39.0 Median : 3.0 Mean : 60.4 Mean : 712.9 3rd Qu.: 54.0 3rd Qu.: 939.0 Max. :320.0 Max. :6711.0

Here with "-" instead of NAs
 > head(occmatx)
[,14] [,15] [,16] [,17] [,18] [,19] [,20] [,21] [1,] "0" "0" "0" "-" "-" "-" "-" "-" [2,] "0" "0" "0" "-" "-" "-" "-" "-" [3,] "0" "0" "-" "-" "-" "-" "-" "-" [4,] "0" "0" "0" "0" "-" "-" "-" "-" [5,] "0" "0" "1" "0" "0" "0" "-" "-" [6,] "0" "0" "0" "0" "0" "0" "-" "-"

> head(stands) age_surv dist_of_s 1 31 646 2 27 0 3 97 0 4 27 2 5 28 27 6 56 0  

> rtv_umf <- unmarkedMultFrame(y=occmatx, siteCovs = stands, numPrimary = 4) > summary(rtv_umf)
unmarkedFrame Object 63 sites Maximum number of observations per site: 116 Mean number of observations per site: 116 Number of primary survey periods: 4 Number of secondary survey periods: 29 Sites with at least one detection: 27 Tabulation of y observations: - 0 1 4533 2683 92 Site-level covariates: age_surv dist_of_s Min. : 21.0 Min. : 0.0 1st Qu.: 28.5 1st Qu.: 0.0 Median : 39.0 Median : 3.0 Mean : 60.4 Mean : 712.9 3rd Qu.: 54.0 3rd Qu.: 939.0 Max. :320.0 Max. :6711.0
Any help would be greatly appreciated! Thanks. 

-Jason

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] NA issue with unmarkedMultFrame
parts:
occmatx should be numeric (0, 1, NA), but based on the output you show, it looks like it is a matrix of character strings ("0", "1", "NA"). If that's the case you should convert all the elements to numeric with code like

occmatx_new <- matrix(as.numeric(occmatx), ncol=ncol(occmatx))

double checking of course that everything was converted correctly.

Ken
